item.title: Integrable turbulence and statistical properties of chaotic wave fields in the complex modified Korteweg-de Vries equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.32397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates integrable turbulence and the mechanism for generating rogue waves in the complex modified Korteweg--de Vries (mKdV) equation through numerical simulations and statistical analysis. We solve the Lax pair eigenvalue problem using the Fourier collocation method and establish a correspondence among solitons, breathers, and rogue waves on the spectral plane. We generate chaotic wave fields by simulating the complex mKdV equation using the split-step Fourier method, starting from a plane wave with superimposed random noise. We analyze the effects of the standard deviation \(\mu\) and the correlation length \(L_c\). The results show that increasing \(\mu\) drives a transition from breather turbulence to soliton turbulence, increasing the probability of rogue-wave generation.In contrast, \(L_c\) primarily influences the spatial scale of the structures. As the constant background of the complex mKdV equation is modulationally stable, its integrable turbulence does not depend on modulational instability. Compared with the nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation under identical initial conditions, the complex mKdV equation attains comparable amplitudes under strong perturbations, but exhibits a higher spatial gradient. This suggests that third-order dispersion and derivative nonlinearity alter the excitation mechanism and steepen the waveform.
item.dc:creator: Ya-Xin Luo, Xiao-Wang Lan, Wei-Qi Peng

item.title: Commuting Families of Flag Quasideterminants in Reflection Equation Algebras of Type A
item.description: arXiv:2610.32521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a family of northeastern antidiagonal quasideterminants associated with the successive blocks of the generating matrix of a reflection equation (RE) algebra of type $A_{n-1}$. Our main result proves the conjecture on their pairwise commutativity formulated earlier. The proof uses the triangular realization of the RE algebra in a quantum enveloping algebra and the flag property of quasideterminants. We also discuss the interpretation of these elements in terms of quantum cluster coordinates and their possible connection with generalized Toda systems.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry V. Talalaev

item.title: Spin Toda systems and N-point spherical Whittaker functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32149v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define and study a spin version of the open Toda integrable system, using the Iwasawa decomposition of a connected split real Lie group. We study spherical Whittaker functions as solutions of the spin Toda system. We also construct their N-point version and find the corresponding factorisation of the Casimir element, which yields asymptotic boundary KZB type equations.
item.dc:creator: Haoyi Li

item.title: Hyperelliptic sigma solutions of polynomial Hamiltonian systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.22784v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study polynomial Hamiltonian systems whose Hamiltonians consist of two weighted products of canonical modes minus a polynomial in their powers. This class extends the structure of familiar genus-one coupled-mode systems from nonlinear optics. We construct local analytic solutions in terms of sigma functions and Abelian integrals on smooth odd-degree hyperelliptic curves, subject to stated regularity conditions. We associate Onishi's determinant identities with the conservation-law structure of these systems, extending the connection previously identified between Frobenius-Stickelberger determinants and conserved quantities in genus-one nonlinear optics. Explicit genus-two and genus-three examples include bounded oscillatory scalar motion. We also classify the Hamiltonian polynomials that eliminate the additional mode exponentials and show that their elementary modes solve second-order equations with self-generating polynomial potentials. We evaluate the solutions using Generapy, a purpose-built Python package for algebraic curves and Abelian functions, and validate them against independent fourth-order Runge-Kutta integration.
item.dc:creator: Graham Hesketh

item.title: Classical elliptic ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model: relation to Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostat and 1-site classical XYZ model with boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2601.06826v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a description of the classical elliptic ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model with 8 independent coupling constants through a pair of ${\rm BC}_1$ type classical Sklyanin algebras generated by the (classical) quadratic reflection equation with non-dynamical XYZ $r$-matrix. For this purpose, we consider the classical version of the $L$-operator for the Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model proposed by O. Chalykh. In ${\rm BC}_1$ case it is factorized to the product of two Lax matrices depending on 4 constants. Then we apply an IRF-Vertex type gauge transformation and obtain a product of the Lax matrices for the Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostats. Each of them is described by the ${\rm BC}_1$ version of the classical Sklyanin algebra. In particular case, when 4 pairs of constants coincide, the ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model exactly coincides with the relativistic Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostat. Explicit change of variables is obtained. We also consider another special case of the ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model with 7 independent constants. We show that it can be reproduced by considering the transfer matrix of the classical 1-site XYZ chain with boundaries. In the end of the paper, using another gauge transformation we represent the Chalykh's Lax matrix in a form depending on the Sklyanin's generators.
item.dc:creator: A. Mostovskii, A. Zotov
